name: Tirana
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Tirana: real estate and developer diligence, public procurement risk, ownership research and dispute support.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Tirana, scoped from Nashville: research on developers, investors and the sources of funds behind the capital's construction boom, background checks on counterparties in public contracts and concessions, and factual support for counsel in commercial and asset recovery matters.
intro: Tirana is Albania's capital and its dominant economic centre. Albania's statistics institute, INSTAT, reports that the Tirana region generates about one third of national GDP, and the city concentrates the national government, the central bank, the main commercial banks, the largest companies and most foreign investors. Construction has been the most visible driver: nationally it reached 12.5 percent of GDP in 2024, its highest level since 2013, with the wave of new towers in Tirana and along the coast cited as a cause. Tourism and services have grown alongside it. Yet local reporting on INSTAT data notes that the city's population rose by only about 1,700 people in 2024, a gap that draws attention to who is financing and buying new buildings.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Tirana for reasons that follow from that profile. Buyers, lenders and joint venture partners in real estate need to know who stands behind developers and investors, and whether funds have a legitimate origin. Public contracts, concessions and public-private partnerships are awarded from the capital, so procurement integrity and political exposure are recurring questions. The work of Albania's special anti-corruption prosecutors and courts, based in Tirana, has put senior officials and business figures under investigation, which matters for counterparty and reputational screening. Creditors and claimants also need lawfully documented facts about assets and related parties.

matters.title: Developer and investor background research
matters.text: Researching the ownership, related companies, project history, litigation and media profile of Tirana developers and the investors behind them, so buyers, lenders and partners can judge reliability and whether the sources of capital raise money laundering or reputational concerns.

matters.title: Public contract and concession risk
matters.text: Background research on companies bidding for or holding public contracts, concessions and public-private partnerships awarded from Tirana, covering beneficial ownership, political exposure, past awards, investigations and adverse media, to support integrity due diligence by financiers, partners and bidders.

matters.title: Politically exposed person screening
matters.text: Identifying links between Tirana counterparties and public officials, their families and associates, and checking whether any are named in SPAK investigations or special court proceedings, so compliance teams can apply enhanced due diligence and document their decisions.

matters.title: Property title and encumbrance questions
matters.text: Assembling publicly available information about plots and buildings in Tirana, including registered owners, disputes and the companies involved in development, to help counsel focus formal cadastre searches where title history or competing claims are a concern.

matters.title: Asset research for creditors
matters.text: Locating lawfully documented company interests, property and related parties of Albanian debtors for creditors and counsel, and identifying transfers to family members or new entities that may need to be addressed in Tirana court proceedings or enforcement.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Tirana
local_context.text: As the capital, Tirana hosts the main first-instance and appeal courts handling commercial disputes for the region, as well as the Supreme Court and the Constitutional Court. The special first-instance and appeal courts against corruption and organised crime (GJKKO), created under the 2016 justice reform, also sit in the city. Litigation and criminal proceedings involving a counterparty therefore often run through Tirana courts.

local_context.title: SPAK and special courts
local_context.text: The Special Structure against Corruption and Organised Crime, SPAK, prosecutes high-level corruption and organised crime with the National Bureau of Investigation and brings cases before the GJKKO courts. Its annual reports describe investigations involving senior officials and business people. Public reports of SPAK cases, while not findings of guilt, are an important reference when screening Tirana counterparties for reputational and integrity risk.

local_context.title: Registries and the capital
local_context.text: Company records are kept nationally by the National Business Center (QKB) and property rights by the State Cadastre Agency, but Tirana generates the largest share of filings and the most complex records, given the volume of construction and transfers. Historic property claims from the post-communist period can still affect title, so cadastre information is read alongside court records and counsel's advice.

local_context.title: Construction and real estate exposure
local_context.text: Construction reached 12.5 percent of Albania's GDP in 2024, and Tirana's new high-rise development has outpaced the city's population growth according to reporting on INSTAT data. This has drawn attention from banks, investors and anti-money laundering bodies to the financing of projects and the buyers of units, which is why source-of-funds questions feature in many Tirana real estate matters. Clients should expect these questions.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Tirana, TDSC first defines the question, whether that is a developer's backers, a bidder's links to officials, a counterparty's exposure to SPAK proceedings or a debtor's assets, and then identifies the relevant records, including QKB company filings, cadastre information, court decisions and Albanian-language media. Research is conducted from Nashville, with Italian, Greek and other foreign records where owners or funds originate abroad. Where interviews, site visits or certified records are needed, TDSC coordinates with appropriately qualified local professionals and the client's Albanian counsel. Personal data is handled in line with Albania's data protection law, and media reports of investigations are presented as allegations, not findings.

faqs.q: How can we check who is behind a Tirana real estate developer?
faqs.a: We review QKB records of partners, administrators and declared beneficial owners, then trace those people and entities through related companies, foreign registries, court decisions and Albanian-language media. Where funding appears to come from abroad or from unexplained sources, we set out what lawful sources show and what counsel or the bank should ask for directly.

faqs.q: Do you check whether a counterparty is involved in SPAK cases?
faqs.a: Yes. We review public information on SPAK investigations and GJKKO proceedings, along with media coverage, and report any links to the counterparty, its owners or managers. We distinguish clearly between investigations, charges and convictions, and we do not seek access to non-public prosecution files. Each reference is sourced.

faqs.q: Can you help with diligence on public contracts or concessions in Albania?
faqs.a: We research bidders, contractors and concessionaires for ownership, political exposure, prior awards, disputes and adverse media, and identify conflicts of interest. This supports integrity due diligence by financiers and partners; questions of procurement law and contract validity are matters for Albanian counsel. We also flag gaps in available records.

faqs.q: Are Tirana property records enough to confirm title?
faqs.a: They are an essential starting point but not always enough. Title history in Tirana can be affected by restitution claims, informal construction and disputes. We assemble the public information and identify issues, while formal cadastre searches and title opinions are obtained through Albanian counsel and notaries.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office in Tirana?
faqs.a: No. TDSC is based in Nashville and has no office or staff in Albania. Most work is desk-based research. Where local steps are justified, we coordinate with appropriately qualified local professionals and the client's Albanian counsel, and we do not use covert or deceptive methods or seek restricted government records.
